why: This week is Math + Arrays. It is an argmax scan, and the only maths is comparing fractions without floating point: r_i/p_i > r_b/p_b becomes r_i*p_b > r_b*p_i because all values are positive.
hints: Keep the index of the best item seen so far.
Compare ratios by cross-multiplying instead of dividing, which avoids floating-point ties.
Replace the best only on a strictly greater ratio, which keeps the lowest index on ties. O(n).
pitfalls: Use a strict '>' so that equal ratios keep the earlier index.
Floating-point division can treat equal ratios such as 1/3 and 2/6 as different. Cross-multiplication is exact.
statement:
You are given two arrays of positive integers of the same length: prices and ratings (each rating is 1 to 5). Item i has value ratings[i] / prices[i]. Return the index of the item with the highest ratio. If several items share the highest ratio, return the smallest index.

Example: prices = [7, 5, 2, 11], ratings = [3, 4, 1, 3].

  • Ratios: 3/7 ≈ 0.43, 4/5 = 0.8, 1/2 = 0.5, 3/11 ≈ 0.27.
  • The largest is 0.8 at index 1.
constraints: • Not stated in the source (it only allows up to O(n³)). Assume 1 ≤ prices.length = ratings.length ≤ 105, 1 ≤ prices[i] ≤ 109, 1 ≤ ratings[i] ≤ 5.
